body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{crit}}\) establish, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\), that the variable-coefficient smoothed gradient Green response has the frozen-pole logarithmic covariance, that the second elliptic term of \(\mathcal D_P\) and its harmonic term \(\mathcal H_P\) have bounded \(L^2\) scores, that coefficient, pole, and selected-lift plug-in errors are \(o(L_n^{1/2})\) in score norm, and that the nonlinear nested remainder is \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\)?
body.justification: This remains the first-class analytic bottleneck; fixed-center annular control is insufficient for random transformed kernels and moving estimated poles.
body.gap: A proof must deliver normalized score stability and the nonlinear tame remainder uniformly over the model class, rather than assuming them from map consistency.
body.consumer: Its resolution is required before the covariance, Gaussian limit, adjoint inference, ellipse coverage, and uniform upper-risk claims can close.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniformly prove the transformed-kernel variable-coefficient Green covariance and \(o(\sqrt{L_n})\) score stability under estimated coefficients and moving poles, together with the \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\) nonlinear nested remainder.
obligation.obstruction: The fixed-center annular resolvent bound does not control a bandwidth-scale random pole displacement. Pointwise coefficient consistency is insufficient because a pole error comparable to \(h_n\) changes the singular score at leading order. The frozen results provide the exact derivative and bandwidth arithmetic but not this uniform stochastic stability or the required mixed tame estimate.
obligation.attempted: The coefficient was frozen at a deterministic pole, the anisotropic fundamental solution was subtracted on dyadic annuli, and the uniform-law Fourier case was evaluated. These close the deterministic fixed-center lower-bound construction and the constant-coefficient check, but they do not justify replacing full transformed KDE scores by frozen-pole scores.
obligation.partial_result:
At a fixed center and a deterministic annular tangent, freezing \(B\) at a fixed pole gives the anisotropic logarithmic fundamental solution
\[
-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B(y)}}\log|B(y)^{-1/2}(z-y)|,
\]
whose gradient has squared mass proportional to \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\).  The proof of lem:green-local-alternatives controls this fixed-center response and its selected translations.  The uniform-law Fourier calculation in prop:uniform-reduction also gives the exact constant \(I_2/(4\pi)\) per sampled cell.  These facts do not control a data-dependent transformed KDE, estimated coefficient, or moving pole uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).
